001package io.github.ai4ci.util;
002
003import java.io.Serializable;
004import java.lang.reflect.Array;
005import java.util.Arrays;
006import java.util.Spliterator;
007import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;
008import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
009import java.util.function.Consumer;
010import java.util.stream.Stream;
011import java.util.stream.StreamSupport;
012
013/**
014 * A thread-safe, dynamically growing array designed for a write-once-read-many
015 * (WORM) pattern.
016 *
017 * <p>
018 * Writes can be performed concurrently from multiple threads using
019 * {@link #put(Object)}. Once all writes are complete, call {@link #finish()} to
020 * seal the array and obtain an immutable, fixed-size snapshot for reading.
021 * </p>
022 *
023 * <p>
024 * This structure assumes two distinct phases:
025 * <ol>
026 * <li><strong>Writing phase:</strong> Multiple threads may call
027 * {@link #put(Object)} or {@link #update(int,Object)} concurrently.</li>
028 * <li><strong>Reading phase:</strong> After calling {@link #finish()}, only
029 * read operations are allowed via {@link #get(int)}, or streaming methods like
030 * {@link #stream()} and {@link #parallelStream()}.</li>
031 * </ol>
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * The array is dynamically resized if needed during writes. Resizing is rare
035 * and synchronized internally, but has minimal impact on throughput when the
036 * final size is preallocated.
037 * </p>
038 *
039 * <p>
040 * {@link #finish()} blocks until all pending writes have completed before
041 * returning the final array.
042 * </p>
043 *
044 * @param <X> the type of elements stored in this array
045 * @author Rob Challen
046 */
047public class ThreadSafeArray<X> implements Serializable {
048
049        /**
050         * Thrown when attempting to write to a {@link ThreadSafeArray} after it has
051         * been finalized with a call to {@link #finish()}.
052         */
053        public static class ReadOnlyException extends RuntimeException {}
054
055        /**
056         * Thrown when attempting to write to a {@link ThreadSafeArray} while it is
057         * being resized or finalized. This exception is not currently used, but
058         * reserved for future internal use.
059         */
060        public static class WriteOnlyException extends RuntimeException {}
061
062        /**
063         * Creates an empty, thread-safe array of the given type and zero initial
064         * capacity.
065         *
066         * @param type the runtime class of the array elements
067         * @param <Y>  the element type
068         * @return a new empty ThreadSafeArray
069         */
070        public static <Y> ThreadSafeArray<Y> empty(Class<Y> type) {
071                return new ThreadSafeArray<>(type, 0);
072        }
073
074        // volatile boolean[] writtenItems;
075        volatile X[] data = null;
076        // points at the first empty space
077        volatile AtomicInteger pointer;
078        // counts the number of written items
079        volatile AtomicInteger written;
080        // the array is cannot be appended to
081        volatile boolean locked = false;
082
083        // the array is busy doing a bulk operation. Appends or updates will be
084        // onSpinWaited.
085        volatile AtomicBoolean updating = new AtomicBoolean();
086
087        /**
088         * Constructs a new thread-safe array with the given element type and initial
089         * capacity.
090         *
091         * <p>
092         * If the final size is known ahead of time, it is recommended to preallocate
093         * the array to minimize resizing overhead during concurrent writes.
094         * </p>
095         *
096         * @param type the runtime class of the array elements
097         * @param size the initial capacity of the array
098         */
099        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
100        public ThreadSafeArray(Class<X> type, int size) {
101                this.updating.set(true);
102                this.pointer = new AtomicInteger(0);
103                this.written = new AtomicInteger(0);
104                this.data = (X[]) Array.newInstance(type, size);
105                // this.writtenItems = new boolean[size];
106                this.updating.set(false);
107        }
108
109        // internal utility method
110        // p must be from an atomicInteger.incrementAndGet() this means it is
111        // definitely unique across all threads:
112        // This may be a cause for contention as multiple things can be waiting for
113        // increase in size. We mitigate this a bit by doubling the largest needed
114        // size so hopefully not too much waiting will be incurred. Potentially
115        // we could think about a wait/notify on "updating".
116        private void ensureCapacityOrWait(int p) {
117
118                while (p >= this.data.length) {
119                        // many threads may be longer than data.length:
120                        // try and grab updating flag:
121                        if (this.updating.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
122                                // OK. just one thread can be here.
123                                if (this.locked) throw new ReadOnlyException();
124                                // Updating flag is set to true so no writes will occur whilst we
125                                // update.
126                                var newCapacity = Math
127                                        .max(this.data.length * 2, this.pointer.get() * 2 + 16);
128                                // debug System.out.println(newCapacity);
129                                // writtenItems = Arrays.copyOf(writtenItems, newCapacity);
130                                this.data = Arrays.copyOf(this.data, newCapacity);
131                                this.updating.set(false);
132                                // updating.notifyAll();
133
134                        } else {
135                                // park other threads that are trying to ensure capacity
136                                while (p >= this.data.length && this.updating.get()) {
137                                        Thread.onSpinWait();
138                                }
139                        }
140                        // capacity is large enough or updates have finished (and capacity is
141                        // still too small).
142                }
143                // capacity if large enough
144        }
145
146        /**
147         * Finalizes the array size, preventing further additions and returning a
148         * read / update only snapshot of the contents.
149         *
150         * <p>
151         * This method blocks until all concurrent writes in progress have completed.
152         * </p>
153         *
154         * <p>
155         * After calling this method, any further calls to {@link #put(Object)} will
156         * throw a {@link ReadOnlyException}.
157         * </p>
158         *
159         * @return a fixed-size copy of the array containing all elements
160         */
161        public X[] finish() {
162                while (!this.updating.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
163                        Thread.onSpinWait();
164                }
165                // This thread is updating. No more additions should be made.
166                // waits for any lagging writer threads to catch up
167                while (this.written.get() < this.pointer.get()) {
168                        Thread.onSpinWait();
169                }
170
171                // Ensure all threads see the 'locked' update before proceeding
172                synchronized (this) {
173
174                        var p = this.pointer.get();
175                        this.data = Arrays.copyOfRange(this.data, 0, p);
176                        // writtenItems = Arrays.copyOfRange(writtenItems, 0, p);
177                        this.locked = true; // prevent further writes
178                        this.updating.set(false);
179                        // Writer threads that were added after finish was called will
180                        // now throw a ReadOnlyException.
181                        return this.data;
182                }
183
184        }
185
186        /**
187         * Retrieves the element at the specified index. Waiting if necessary until
188         * it is available.
189         *
190         * <p>
191         * If called before {@link #finish()}, this method throws an
192         * {@link ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException} if the element does not yet exist.
193         * </p>
194         *
195         * <p>
196         * Callers should ensure that the index is within bounds as reported by
197         * current write progress (e.g., via {@link #size()}).
198         * </p>
199         *
200         * @param p index of the element to retrieve
201         * @return the element at the given index
202         */
203        public X get(int p) {
204                if (!this.locked) throw new WriteOnlyException();
205                if (p >= this.pointer.get()) throw new ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException();
206                return this.data[p];
207        }
208
209        /**
210         * Checks whether no elements have been written yet.
211         *
212         * @return true if size() == 0
213         */
214        public boolean isEmpty() { return this.size() == 0; }
215
216        /**
217         * Returns a parallel stream of the elements currently visible for reading.
218         *
219         * <p>
220         * Like {@link #stream()}, this reflects the ideal state of the array at the
221         * time of the call. It may have to wait for items to become fully available.
222         * </p>
223         *
224         * @return a parallel stream of the array contents
225         */
226//      public Stream<X> parallelStream() {
227//              if (!this.locked) throw new WriteOnlyException();
228//              int p = this.pointer.get();
229//              return IntStream.range(0, p).parallel().mapToObj(i -> this.get(i));
230//      }
231//      
232        public Stream<X> parallelStream() {
233                if (!this.locked) throw new WriteOnlyException();
234                if (this.isEmpty()) return Stream.empty();
235                return StreamSupport.stream(new ParentSpliterator(), true); // , true);
236        }
237
238        private class ParentSpliterator implements Spliterator<X> {
239
240                AtomicInteger head = new AtomicInteger(0);
241                AtomicInteger splits = new AtomicInteger(1);
242
243                @Override
244                public boolean tryAdvance(Consumer<? super X> action) {
245                        var i = this.head.getAndAdd(1);
246                        if (i >= ThreadSafeArray.this.size()) return false;
247                        action.accept(ThreadSafeArray.this.data[i]);
248                        return true;
249                }
250
251                @Override
252                public Spliterator<X> trySplit() {
253                        return new ChildSpliterator(this);
254                }
255
256                @Override
257                public long estimateSize() {
258                        return (ThreadSafeArray.this.size() - this.head.get())
259                                        / this.splits.get();
260                }
261
262                @Override
263                public int characteristics() {
264                        return Spliterator.IMMUTABLE + Spliterator.NONNULL + Spliterator.SIZED;
265                }
266
267        }
268
269        private class ChildSpliterator implements Spliterator<X> {
270
271                ParentSpliterator parent;
272
273                ChildSpliterator(ParentSpliterator parent) {
274                        this.parent = parent;
275                        parent.splits.incrementAndGet();
276                }
277
278                @Override
279                public boolean tryAdvance(Consumer<? super X> action) {
280                        return this.parent.tryAdvance(action);
281                }
282
283                @Override
284                public Spliterator<X> trySplit() {
285                        return new ChildSpliterator(this.parent);
286                }
287
288                @Override
289                public long estimateSize() {
290                        return this.parent.estimateSize();
291                }
292
293                @Override
294                public int characteristics() {
295                        return Spliterator.IMMUTABLE + Spliterator.NONNULL;
296                }
297        }
298
299        /**
300         * Adds an element to the array.
301         *
302         * <p>
303         * This method is safe to call from multiple threads concurrently. If the
304         * internal array needs resizing, only one thread will perform the resize
305         * operation while others wait.
306         * </p>
307         *
308         * @param value the element to add
309         * @return the index at which the element was inserted
310         * @throws ReadOnlyException if called after {@link #finish()}
311         */
312        public int put(X value) {
313                if (this.locked) throw new ReadOnlyException();
314                while (this.updating.get()) {
315                        Thread.onSpinWait();
316                }
317                if (this.locked) throw new ReadOnlyException();
318                var p = this.pointer.getAndIncrement();
319                this.ensureCapacityOrWait(p);
320                this.data[p] = value;
321                // this.writtenItems[p] = true;
322                this.written.getAndIncrement();
323                return p;
324        }
325
326        /**
327         * Returns the number of elements successfully written so far.
328         *
329         * <p>
330         * This value may be less than the actual array capacity due to dynamic
331         * resizing.
332         * </p>
333         *
334         * @return the current count of written elements
335         */
336        public int size() {
337                return this.pointer.get();
338        }
339
340        /**
341         * Returns a sequential stream of the elements currently visible for reading.
342         *
343         * <p>
344         * The stream reflects the ideal state of the array at the time of the call.
345         * It may have to wait for all items to become available.
346         * </p>
347         *
348         * @return a sequential stream of the array contents
349         */
350        public Stream<X> stream() {
351                if (!this.locked) throw new WriteOnlyException();
352                if (this.isEmpty()) return Stream.empty();
353                return StreamSupport.stream(new ParentSpliterator(), true);
354        }
355
356        /**
357         * Updates the value at the specified index, assuming the value already
358         * exists, and the initial loading phase is complete but the array has not
359         * been finalised.
360         *
361         * <p>
362         * This method is thread-safe and supports concurrent writes to different
363         * indices.
364         * </p>
365         *
366         * @param index the index at which to update the element
367         * @param value the element to update
368         * @throws ReadOnlyException         if called after the array has been
369         *                                   finalized
370         * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if the index is out of bounds
371         */
372        public void update(int index, X value) {
373                if (this.locked) throw new ReadOnlyException();
374                // Wait for any ongoing resize
375                while (this.updating.get()) {
376                        Thread.onSpinWait();
377                }
378                // Write the value, will throw index out of bounds if index invalid
379                if (index >= this.pointer.get()) throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException();
380                // while (!writtenItems[index]) Thread.onSpinWait();
381                // Array update is atomic, so no need for additional synchronization here
382                this.data[index] = value;
383                // redundant writtenItems.set(index);
384        }
